dhpak1.15:1.1: 1.14 The Story about Two Monastic Friends Dvesahayakabhikkhūnaṁ Vatthu
dhpak1.15:2.1: “Even though reciting abundant scriptures,” {1.154} this Dhamma teaching was given by
dhpak1.15:2.2: the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to two fellow bhikkhus.
dhpak1.15:3.1: For at Sāvatthī lived two young men of station who were inseparable friends. On a certain occasion they
dhpak1.15:3.2: went to the monastery, heard the Teacher teach the Dhamma, renounced the pleasures of the world,
dhpak1.15:3.3: gave their hearts to the dispensation of the Buddha, and went forth. When they had kept residence for five
dhpak1.15:3.4: years with preceptors and teachers, they approached the Teacher and asked about the duties in his dispensation.
dhpak1.15:4.1: After listening to a detailed description of the duty of meditation and of the duty of study, one of them said: “Venerable Sir,
dhpak1.15:4.2: since I went forth in old age, I shall not be able to fulfill the duty of study, but I can fulfill the duty of meditation.”
dhpak1.15:5.1: So he had [28.245] the Teacher instruct him in the duty of meditation as far as Arahatship, and after striving and struggling
dhpak1.15:5.2: attained Arahatship, together with the analytic knowledges. But the other said: “I will fulfill the duty of study,”
dhpak1.15:5.3: and acquired by degrees the Three Baskets, the word of the Buddha, and wherever he went, taught the Dhamma and intoned it.
dhpak1.15:5.4: He went from place to place reciting the Dhamma to five hundred bhikkhus, and was preceptor of eighteen large communities of bhikkhus.
dhpak1.15:6.1: Striving and Struggling Now a company of bhikkhus, having obtained a meditation subject from the Teacher, went to the place
dhpak1.15:6.2: of residence of the older bhikkhu, and by faithful observance of his admonitions attained Arahatship.
dhpak1.15:6.3: Thereupon they worshipped the elder and said: “We desire to see the Teacher.” {1.155} The Elder said: “Go, friends,
dhpak1.15:6.4: greet in my name the Teacher, and likewise greet the eighty great elders, and greet my fellow elder, saying: ‘Our Teacher greets you.’”
dhpak1.15:6.5: So those bhikkhus went to the monastery and greeted the Teacher and the elders, saying: “Venerable Sir, our teacher greets you.”
dhpak1.15:6.6: When they greeted their teacher’s fellow elder, he replied: “Who is he?” Said the bhikkhus: “He is your fellow bhikkhu, venerable Sir.”
dhpak1.15:7.1: Said the younger bhikkhu: “But what have you learned from him? Of the Collection of Long Discourses and so on,
dhpak1.15:7.2: have you learned a single Collection? Of the Three Baskets, have you learned a single Basket?” And he thought to himself:
dhpak1.15:7.3: “This bhikkhu does not know a single verse containing four lines. As soon as he went forth, he took rags from a dust-heap,
dhpak1.15:7.4: entered the forest, and gathered a great many pupils about him. When he returns, it is necessary for me to ask him some questions.”
dhpak1.15:8.1: Now somewhat later the older bhikkhu came to see the Teacher, and leaving his bowl and robe with his fellow elder,
dhpak1.15:8.2: went and greeted the Teacher and the eighty great elders, afterwards returning to the place of residence of his fellow elder.
dhpak1.15:8.3: The younger bhikkhu showed him the customary attentions, provided him with a seat of the
dhpak1.15:8.4: same size as his own, and then sat down, thinking to himself: “I will ask him a question.”
dhpak1.15:9.1: At that moment the Teacher thought to himself: “Should this bhikkhu annoy this my son, he is likely to be reborn in Niraya Hell.”
dhpak1.15:9.2: So out of compassion for him, pretending to be going the rounds of the monastery,
dhpak1.15:9.3: he went to the place where the two bhikkhus were sitting and sat down on the Buddha seat already prepared.
dhpak1.15:10.1: For wherever the bhikkhus sit down, they first prepare the seat of the Buddha, and not until they have so
dhpak1.15:10.2: done do they themselves sit down. {1.156} Therefore the Teacher sat down on a seat already prepared for him.
dhpak1.15:11.1: And when [28.246] he had sat down, he asked the bhikkhu who had taken upon himself the duty of study a question about the first absorption.
dhpak1.15:11.2: When the younger bhikkhu had answered this question correctly, the Teacher, beginning with the second absorption,
dhpak1.15:11.3: asked him questions about the eight attainments and about the form and the formless worlds, all of which he answered correctly.
dhpak1.15:12.1: Then the Teacher asked him a question about Stream-entry, and he was unable to answer it.
dhpak1.15:12.2: Thereupon the Teacher asked the bhikkhu who was an Arahat, and the latter immediately gave the correct answer. “Well done,
dhpak1.15:12.3: well done, bhikkhu!” said the Teacher, greatly pleased. The Teacher then asked questions about the remaining paths in order.
dhpak1.15:13.1: The bhikkhu who had taken upon himself the duty of study was unable to answer a single question, while the bhikkhu who had attained
dhpak1.15:13.2: unto Arahatship answered every question he asked. On each of four occasions the Teacher bestowed applause on him. Hearing this,
dhpak1.15:13.3: all the Devas, from the Bhummadevas to the world of Brahma, all Devatās, including Nāgas and Supaṇṇas, shouted their applause.
dhpak1.15:14.1: Hearing this applause, the pupils and fellow-residents of the younger bhikkhu were offended at the Teacher and said:
dhpak1.15:14.2: “Why did the Teacher do this? He bestowed applause on each of four occasions on the old bhikkhu who knows nothing at all.
dhpak1.15:14.3: But to our own teacher, who knows all the sacred word by heart and is at the head of five hundred bhikkhus, he gave no praise at all.”
dhpak1.15:15.1: The Teacher asked them: “Bhikkhus, what is it you are talking about?” When they told him, he said: “Bhikkhus,
dhpak1.15:15.2: your own teacher is in my dispensation like a man who tends cows for hire. But my son is like a master who enjoys
dhpak1.15:15.3: the five products of the cow at his own good pleasure.” So saying, he pronounced the following verses: {1.157}
dhpak1.15:16.1: The Teacher Explains... 19. Bahum-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno,
dhpak1.15:16.2: na takkaro hoti naro pamatto, gopo va gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
dhpak1.15:17.1: Even though reciting abundant scriptures, the heedless one, who does not what they say,
dhpak1.15:17.2: like a cowboy counting other’s cattle, does not partake of the ascetic life.
dhpak1.15:18.1: 20. Appam-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī, rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca pahāya mohaṁ,
dhpak1.15:18.2: sammappajāno suvimuttacitto, anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā, sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
dhpak1.15:19.1: Even though reciting only few scriptures, but living in accordance with Dhamma, abandoning greed, hate and delusion,
dhpak1.15:19.2: understanding aright, with mind released, that one, unattached here and hereafter, surely partakes of the ascetic life.
dhpak1.15:20.1: At the end of the verse many became Stream-enterers and so on, and benefit arose to many people from the teaching.
